Oxygen-rich aldehydes, esters, aromatic carbonyls, and donor alcohols receive ratio curves and selected loading contrasts because recent labels show that V1 and V2 can move independently. Acid-bearing points map a sharp regime transition. Charged, nitro, fused-nitrogen, sulfur, and heteroaromatic rows probe atom environments that are sparse or poorly transferred from neutral chemistry. Several high-width V2 candidates target completion and interval-width behavior directly, while low-ratio anchors prevent the batch from sampling only the retained tail. These complementary labels should improve generalization across the Row-distribution by teaching condition-structure interactions and repairing systematic endpoint failures rather than merely adding redundant molecules."}
